catalog_quote: [p. 285] Remarque 2. A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement: aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345). [p. 345] Remarque. On pourrait poser que la langue ancestrale ne connaissait que des syllabes ouvertes et un accent: *CV, *CVCV (qui aurait donné CVCV non accentué) et *CVCV (qui aurait donné CVC). L'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles n'impose pas cette solution en proto-gbaya, mais l'hypothèse est envisageable à un niveau antérieur de l'évolution.

new_statements.translation: Remark 2. To the question, raised by Jacqueline Thomas, whether the differences in tonal treatment according to syllable type might be explained by the presence of an accent in the languages concerned, the answer must be negative: none of them at present shows any phenomenon of accent, intensity or length. The hypothesis will be raised again in diachrony, in interpreting the sound correspondences (p. 345). [p. 345:] The absence of accent in the present-day languages does not force this solution for proto-Gbaya, but the hypothesis is conceivable at an earlier stage of the evolution.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The Southwest Gbaya varieties ('buli, 'biyanda, toongo), like all 21 Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka languages Moñino surveyed from his own fieldwork, are two-tone languages (tonal areas a3/a4 in his table) with no accent, intensity or length phenomenon at all; no syllable of the word carries stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned (no stress of any kind).
new_statements.exceptions: None; the statement is blanket over all 21 languages. A word-level accent is only entertained as a hypothesis for a pre-proto-Gbaya stage (p. 345).
new_statements.domain_note: Blanket statement in the contrastive recapitulation of a comparative work, made for the whole group of 21 languages, not in a variety-specific phonology section; the tonal contrast at issue concerns tone-sandhi (marqueur de relation) behaviour by syllable type across lexical/phrasal domains. First-hand (Moñino's own 1970-73 data, pp. 51-52), but the individual chapters on 'biyanda, 'buli and toongo (Part I) were not obtained. Confidence medium for that reason.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is a blanket remark in Moñino 1995 covering all 21 Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka languages of his survey; the Southwest Gbaya [gso] varieties it covers are gbaya 'buli and 'biyanda (row a4 of the p. 285 table) and toongo (row a3), collected by Moñino himself in 1970-73 ('Biyanda of Kui-So, 'Buli of Date, toongo at Zu-Kombo; pp. 51-52). Glottolog ref 116367 maps these to Gbaya Buli / Biyanda / Toongo [gso]. Glottolog sout2785 has no dialect glottocodes; Wikipedia treats it as 'Biyanda-Buli' (+ Toongo). Caution on neighbours: Moñino's 'gbaya kara' and 'yaayuwee', Roulon-Doko's 'bodoe, and Noss's Yaayuwee grammar/dictionary are Northwest Gbaya [gya] = nort2775 (confirmed by Roulon-Doko & Dui 2024, p. 1); Mbodomo is gmm = gbay1281; Gbeya/Samarin and Ruckstuhl are gbp = gbay1287. Hartmann 1930 (assigned by Glottolog to Gbaya Buli, gso) describes the 'western' (Cameroon-side) Baja with only a notation convention for Betonung.

new_statements.translation: Remark 2. To the question, raised by Jacqueline Thomas, whether the differences in tonal treatment according to syllable type might be explained by the presence of an accent in the languages concerned, one must answer in the negative: none of them currently shows any phenomenon of accent, intensity or length. The hypothesis will be raised again in the diachronic part, in the interpretation of the sound correspondences (p. 345). || [p. 345] Remark. One could posit that the ancestral language had only open syllables and an accent: *CV, *CVCV (which would have given unaccented CVCV) and *CVCV (which would have given CVC). The absence of accent in the present-day languages does not force this solution for Proto-Gbaya, but the hypothesis is conceivable at an earlier stage of the evolution.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The Gbaya languages surveyed, including toongo (table row a3) and 'buli and 'biyanda (row a4), are tone languages with no word accent: no stress, intensity or length phenomenon exists synchronically; tonal alternations by syllable type are not accent-driven. An accent is only entertained as a possible pre-Proto-Gbaya diachronic stage.
new_statements.exceptions: None. Remarque 2's 'aucune' refers to 'les langues concernées' = the area-a languages of the table, which explicitly include toongo, 'buli and 'biyanda; p. 345 generalises to 'les langues actuelles' (all 21 languages surveyed).
new_statements.identity_note: Moñino 1995 treats 'biyanda, 'buli and toongo as three separate languages of his 21-language Gbaya survey (own fieldwork 1970-73: 'Biyanda of Kui-So, 'Buli of Date, toongo of Zu-Kombo, pp. 51-52); all three map to Glottolog sout2785 (Southwest Gbaya [gso]). The p. 285 table names them individually (toongo in row a3; 'buli and 'biy[anda] in row a4), so the no-accent statement covers all three varieties of this glottocode explicitly. Noss's and Roulon-Doko's Gbaya works concern Yaayuwee/'bodoe = Northwest Gbaya (nort2775), not this item.

Useful for identity: 'Le gbaya Northwest (ISO : GYA; nort2775; WALS gbk).. comporte cinq dialectes : quatre en RCA [ɓòdòè, ɓòkpàn, ɓòɲìnà, ɓùgùì].. et un au Cameroun le yàáyùwèè' (p. 1); 'C'est une langue tonale avec deux niveaux et quatre tons' (p. 2). In MAYOGO there is a tendency towards vowel length on the penultimate syllable. In NGBAKA, GBAYA, and BANDA, on the other hand, there is a tendency towards extra shortness here.'
